main_html:
EBV is a first-of-its-kind initiative that turns veterans into entrepreneurs! The EBV program leverages the skills, resources and infrastructure of higher education to offer cutting-edge, experiential training in entrepreneurship and small business management to post-9/11 veterans.

About EBV

The EBV, founded at Syracuse University in 2007, opens the door to economic opportunity for veterans by developing their competencies in the many steps and activities associated with creating and sustaining an entrepreneurial venture. This exclusive cohort, hosted in partnership with Wounded Warrior Project, will provide opportunities to meet warriors where they are at in the early stages of their entrepreneurship journey.

This program is powered in part by Wounded Warrior Project to honor and empower post-9/11 injured service members, veterans, and their families.

What You Will Experience

  • World class entrepreneurship training with fellow veterans (or family members)
  • Lifelong mentors and friends established at the course
  • A community of like-minded entrepreneurs, veterans and program graduates

Length

  • Phase I: Four-week online, instructors-led business fundamentals and research course work
  • Phase II: Five-day, in-person residency experience
  • Phase III: 12-month ongoing support focused on small business creation and growth

Eligibility

Post 9/11 veterans with Honorable discharge who are WWP alumni.

No Cost

The entire EBV experience, including travel and lodging, is offered without any cost to participating Veterans

Contact

Email: IVMFEducation@syr.edu
Phone: (315) 443-6898

Program Schedule

Veteran EDGE (Engage. Develop. Grow. Elevate.) is a four-day conference dedicated solely to veteran and military spouse business owners and the ecosystem that supports them.

Learn more

EBV Accelerate

Accelerate is a bootcamp-style program focused on growth and tackles head-on topics such as the financial, management, marketing and strategic planning challenges established businesses face.

Learn more

CEOcircle

CEOcircle is a monthly peer accountability group for growth-stage companies looking to scale. Over the course of nine virtual huddles and four in person fly-in forum events, CEOs and executives can ask critical questions impacting their businesses today.

Because scaling a business isn’t guesswork. It’s strategy, execution, and the right network.

Veteran EDGE is designed for entrepreneurs leading established companies earning at least $100K+ in annual revenue, with preference given to those generating $500K and above, who are ready to grow, pivot, or expand into new market.

  • Proven Growth Strategies Breakouts and workshops on advanced sales, storytelling, procurement readiness, mergers & acquisitions, exit planning, creative problem solving, AI adoption, and cutting-edge marketing.
  • Unmatched Access: One-on-one meetings with corporate decision makers, government contracting leaders, subject matter experts, and resource providers.
  • Strategic Business Networks: Industry Night, networking receptions, and peer-to-peer sessions designed to connect you with partners, clients, and suppliers who can move your business forward.
  • Direct Revenue Generation: Showcase, and even sell, your products or services at the Business Showcase Expo!

What Makes EDGE Different

Veteran EDGE isn’t another conference; it’s a growth accelerator in action. For three days, you’ll be immersed in hard-hitting strategy, insider industry insights, and curated networking that drives results. From the high-energy keynotes to the Business Showcase and one-on-one coaching with experts, every moment is engineered to spark opportunities that turn into deals, partnerships, and revenue.

Vet100

Veteran EDGE is the official stage for the annual Vet100 Dinner & Awards, presented in partnership with Inc. Business Media and powered by Fiserv.

Vet100 recognizes the 100 fastest-growing veteran- and military-spouse-owned businesses in America, spotlighting entrepreneurs who are leading industries nationwide. This event is more than an awards dinner. It is a celebration and a networking hub for top-performing military-connected companies.

Learn more about the Vet100

D’Aniello Family Foundation Acceleration Challenge

Participants (ten total) will be nominated to participate in a series of activities and workshops to assess the barriers confronting their business and best prepare them to leverage the resources of the conference. They will be eligible to apply for up to $10,000 in grant funding for their company!

Details

Who

Veteran EDGE brings together high-performing veteran and military-connected entrepreneurs leading established companies. Businesses earning $100K+ in annual revenue are encouraged to apply, with preference given to those generating $500K and above.

What

A three-day business growth conference designed exclusively for veteran- and spouse-owned companies. Your registration fee includes three nights of lodging, full access to all sessions and networking events, and most meals during the event.

Why

Because launching is only the beginning, scaling is your next challenge. Veteran EDGE was created to fill the gap with advanced workshops, breakout sessions, and networking opportunities led by industry experts and national partners including Walmart, JPMorgan Chase, Fiserv, Wells Fargo, Department of War, NVSBC, and more.

When

Veteran EDGE meets once a year for three days in March.

Where

Dallas, TX

Are you ready to make an impact at Veteran EDGE?

Corporate, government, and philanthropic partners connect directly with high-growth business owners at EDGE who are scaling, hiring, and shaping the future of the U.S. economy. Your partnership fuels access to education, conversations, capital, mentorship, procurement opportunities, and measurable impact across the veteran entrepreneurship ecosystem.

Learn how your organization can support EDGE 2026 through sponsorship, collaboration, or thought leadership opportunities.

FAQ

  • Who is eligible to participate?

    Participants must be business owners in operation for at least one year with annual revenues of $100,000 or more (with preference for those exceeding $500,000). They must also be either a veteran with an honorable discharge or a military spouse/partner.

  • What is Veteran EDGE?

    Veteran EDGE is a three-day, in-person business growth conference designed to help veteran and military spouse entrepreneur’s scale. The registration fee includes full access to sessions, workshops, and networking events, plus three nights of lodging and most meals.

  • When does EDGE take place?

    Veteran EDGE is held annually in March.

  • Where is EDGE held?

    The conference takes place in Dallas, Texas.

  • Why should I attend?

    While there are many programs to help launch a business, very few focus on scaling. EDGE fills that gap by providing strategies, resources, and connections to accelerate growth. The conference features breakout sessions, workshops, networking opportunities, and keynotes from leaders at organizations like JPMorgan Chase, Fiserv, the U.S. Department of War, and the National Veteran Small Business Coalition.

  • Can I attend more than once?

    Yes, though the registration fee is required each time.

  • Do I have to be an IVMF or Bunker Labs member/alumni?

    No. Anyone who meets the eligibility requirements may apply.

  • What costs are involved?

    The registration fee covers conference access, three nights of lodging, and most meals and non-alcoholic beverages. Participants are responsible for their own travel.

  • How many attendees are there?

    The conference brings together 400+ attendees, including participants, corporate partners, resource providers, instructors, and other key stakeholders.

  • How are participants selected?

    Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis to ensure eligibility. Businesses with revenues over $500,000 are preferred until capacity is reached.

  • Does IVMF invest in EDGE businesses?

    No, IVMF does not directly invest capital. However, alumni businesses gain access to ongoing support, resources, and visibility through initiatives like the IVMF Buy Military Shopping Guide.

  • Do I need to be a veteran to apply?

    You must be either a military veteran with an honorable discharge or a military spouse/partner.

  • If I was not accepted in the past, can I reapply?

    Yes, as long as you now meet the eligibility requirements.

page_title: Entrepreneurship Bootcamp for Veterans Accelerate - D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families
main_html:
Ready to Take Your Business to The Next Level?

EBV Accelerate is a 3-phase program that gives veterans with a successful business the tools and coaching to propel their business to the next phase: sustainable growth. Topics will include acquiring growth funding, rebranding for expansion, determining a sustainable growth rate, establishing partnerships, managing cash flow, and much more.

Length

PHASE 1: two weeks of online instruction focused on business analysis.

PHASE 2: is a three-day residency during which participants will create a personalized action plan for their business.

  • Tuesday-Thursday; Monday & Friday as Travel Days
  • Travel to the location is at the candidate’s cost.
  • Lodging and meals are provided for the participant during the three days of Phase 2.
  • All program learning materials will be provided at no cost to the participant.

PHASE 3: involves resources to support the growth of your business.

Eligibility

  • Open to all Veteran business owners
    • Must have 50% or more ownership maintained by veteran
  • In business for 3 or more years (recommended; must have financials)
  • Must employ 5 or more full-time employees
  • Served active duty with honorable discharge or general discharge under honorable conditions
  • Graduates of other IVMF programs are eligible

Cost

All lodging, meals and program materials are provided at no cost. Participant is responsible for travel to and from the host school.

Contact

Email: IVMFEducation@syr.edu
Phone: (315) 443-6898

Program Schedule

The program is being hosted jointly by Louisiana State University and Florida State University this year. Only one set of dates are being offered in 2025. The residency portion (Phase II) will be held at Louisiana State University.

Program Dates:

Application Deadline: August 28, 2026

Phase I: September 14 – October 2, 2026

Phase II: October 26 – 29, 2026

EBV Impact

79%
 of EBV Graduates have started or
continued to grow their own business

83%
Of those are still in business today

$194M+
the average annual revenue of EBV
graduate businesses.

Entrepreneurship Bootcamp for Veterans (EBV)

Interested in the full program with more locations across the country? Explore all of the EBV offerings with almost 20 years of history in teaching veterans the skills they need to succeed in entrepreneurship. Offered at schools like Texas A&M, UCLA, Syracuse University, and more.

Check out the full EBV program now!

Learn more

EBV Foundation

The EBV Foundation was established in 2009 and works closely with the Entrepreneurship Bootcamp for Veterans consortium as well as graduates of the EBV program. Learn more about the EBV Foundation.

Become A Resource Partner

As EBV graduates launch and grow their ventures, the EBV-Technical Assistance Program (EBV-TAP) team is at the ready with support service. If you would like become a part of our follow-on support team and have resources to provide  please contact us.

Post Program Support

Providing our graduates with the training, networks, and support to successfully launch and grow a business. Learn more at Alumni Resources.

page_title: EBV Accelerate Application - D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families
main_html:
You may begin the application at any time and will have the ability to save and return to edit and complete the application within 30 days.

As part of the application, you will be asked for details about your business such as the industry in which you operate, income or P&L details and the number of employees. For other required documents please see below, note each file has a 5MB size limit for upload:

  • Résumé  (Word or PDF format)
  • DD214 Member 4 (showing dates of active duty, character of service. Please redact the SSN.) (PDF, .png, or .jpeg)
  • Self or accountant-prepared Income Statement OR Profit & Loss Statement (Past 3 years – one document) (Word or PDF format)
  • Letter of recommendation* from a client (Word or PDF format)
  • Letter of recommendation* from someone on your BAIL team (Banker, Accountant, Insurance agent, Legal) OR a Business Partner (Word of PDF format)

*Letters of recommendation need to be current, and speak to your intent to participate in EBV Accelerate, must state the writer’s relationship to your business, and provide writer’s contact information (phone number and/or email). Letters can be waived for EBV graduates, if all other requirements are met.

page_title: Our Programs - D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families
main_html:
Career Training

Onward to Opportunity

A career skills program that provides civilian career training, professional certifications and employment services.

Learn More About O2O

Veterans for Public Office

Training program for veterans and military-connected considering careers in politics.

Learn About VPO

Entrepreneurship

Veteran EDGE

EDGE is a four-day conference dedicated solely to veteran and military spouse business owners and the ecosystem that supports them.

Learn More

V-WISE

A women-focused training program in entrepreneurship and small business management for aspiring women entrepreneurs.

Learn More

CEOcircle

CEOcircle is a monthly peer accountability group for growth-stage companies looking to scale.

Learn More

EBV

A cutting-edge entrepreneurship training program teaching the steps and stages of business creation and business management.

Learn More

EBV Accelerate

Ready to take your business to the next level? EBV Accelerate is a bootcamp-style program focused on growth and tackles various topics head-on.

Learn More 

EBV Families

A Program that integrates training with caregiver and family matters, so participants can launch a small business while tending to family responsibilities.

Learn More

EBV Wounded Warrior Project

An entrepreneurship training program teaching the steps and stages of business creation and management for WWP Alumni.

Learn More

Military Founders Lab

10-week virtual program delivers immediate, practical impact with access to business tools, resources, mentorship, and a strong peer network for veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs.

Learn More

STRIVE

The Startup Training Resources to Inspire Veteran Entrepreneurship (STRIVE) is part of a landmark initiative that transforms military-connected into entrepreneurs.

Learn More

Boots to Business

Leads participants through the key steps for evaluating business concepts and provides the foundational knowledge required to develop a business plan.

Learn More

Military Entrepreneurship Forum

A series of regionally focused entrepreneurship training events designed to connect entrepreneurs with their local business resources and entrepreneurship support partners.

Learn More

Mission to Marketplace

A full-day event that focuses on providing veteran and military spouse owned businesses in that regional area the opportunity to learn from and network with subject matter experts.

Learn More

Community Services

AmericaServes

Provides veterans, transitioning service members, and their families access to a simple and effective way to access and navigate a range of supportive services in their communities.

Learn More

Community of Practice

The Community of Practice is a dedicated learning network dedicated to sharing insights and best practices among community service providers and coordination centers from all over the country.

Learn more

Research, Evaluation and Policy

Applied Research

Conduct independent and sponsored nonpartisan research to identify gaps in knowledge, policy, and practice, and deliver action-oriented solutions for our partners. Our research team informs IVMF programs, guides future direction, and empowers action across the veteran and military-connected community.

Learn More

Evaluation

Oversee program evaluation efforts for the IVMF, lead or assist in evaluation efforts with our partners, and highlight leaders in the field. The work spans a range of evaluation approaches and methods to assess and convey outcomes.

Learn More

Policy

Public policy aimed at supporting veterans is most effective when it’s informed by evidence and experience. The IVMF empowers public sector leaders by translating insights from research and practice into better policymaking.

Learn More

Resources

Coalition for Veteran Owned Business (CVOB)

Is a coalition of private sector companies, businesses, non-governmental organizations (NGOs) working to connect veteran- and military family-owned business to supply chains of medium-sized and large corporations.

Learn More

Center of Excellence for Veteran Entrepreneurship (COE)

The mission of the (COE) is to create, collect, organize, and share knowledge, resources, and networks to advance entrepreneurial opportunities for the military community.

Learn More

Digital Library

Introducing IVMF Digital Library! You can explore IVMF-authored publications as well as several curated topical collections of useful external research, information, and resources.

Learn More

Ambassador Program

The Ambassador Program unites entrepreneurial servant leaders across the country in a mission to build and build up local business ecosystems.

Learn More

Alumni Resources

As a graduate or participant of one of the Institute for Veterans and Military Families’ programs, you are a part of an ever-growing network of IVMF alumni across the globe!

Learn More

VetNet

Free online resource offering innovative networking tools, career training, job opportunities and entrepreneurship classes.

Learn More

Military-Owned Shopping Guide

Shop IVMF’s military-owned shopping guide with over 500 veteran, active duty, reservists and military spouse-owned businesses!

Learn More

Veteran Capital Readiness Initiative (V-CAP)

Whether you are a transitioning service member, veteran, or military spouse, IVMF’s V-CAP connects you to the resources, services, and programs you need to thrive on your entrepreneurial journey.

Learn More

Entrepreneurship Conferences and Pitch Competitions

Conferences and conventions are a great way to expand your network, hear about opportunities, and keep up with current and emerging trends in your industry.

Learn More

IVMF Entrepreneurship Resource Directory

A variety of resources are present in this directory, including a variety of how-to and resource blogs, research and information from the IVMF website, external organization links with programs, resources, or other helpful information.

Learn More

Higher Education

Syracuse University

Syracuse is designated as one of the top Private School for Veterans according to Military Times. The support of military-connected scholars is central to the University’s mission, and includes commitments to affordability, academic success, and a comfortable fit within the student body.

Learn More.

meta_description: Military Founders Lab is a 10-week virtual program delivers immediate, practical impact with access to business tools, resources, mentorship, and a strong peer network for veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs.
main_html:
Formerly the Veterans in Residence (ViR), Breaking Barriers in Entrepreneurship (BBiE), and Bunker Build Up (BBU) programs, IVMF has streamlined and combined these three programs into the Military Founders Lab. Over 10-weeks, this virtual program delivers immediate, practical impact and support for business growth and development with access to business tools, resources, mentorship, and a strong peer network. Military Founders Lab also provides multiple tracks that align participants by shared experiences or industries, creating a tailored support system and stronger connections within each cohort.

What You Will Experience

  • Build and develop business knowledge and management skills
  • Increase confidence to grow a viable, sustainable business
  • Learn about resources and tools to accelerate business growth
  • Expand professional network among like-minded, veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs at a similar stage of business

Eligibility

  • Active-duty, veterans, reservists, guard, military and veteran spouses/life partners/adult dependents/caregivers.
  • All must present documentation of honorable service for self, spouse, partner, parent, or veteran receiving care.
  • All eras and all service branches are eligible.

Applicants must also meet the following business requirements:

  • Have been actively working on business development and operations for at least six months.
  • Have a registered business in their state of operations, including sole proprietorship, partnership, LLC, corporation, or nonprofit organization.
  • Generating revenue under $250K in the last 12 months or not generating revenue but have capital investment (bootstrapped or investor-provided) to fund startup and growth operations.

Program Details

Participants in the Military Founders Lab will actively engage in two virtual meetings per week, accompanied by structured weekly coursework. The Speaker Series (live webinar led by a Subject Matter Expert) is held on Mondays at 2pm ET and is recorded for asynchronous review if needed. If a participant is not able to attend and engage in the Speaker Series live, they are required to review the recording after the fact. The Founders Exchange (live virtual office hour) is track-specific and must be attended and engaged with live – they are not recorded. Participants are required to attend and engage with at least five live Founders Exchange sessions over the course of 10 weeks.

Upcoming Cohorts

There are three, 10-week, Military Founders Lab cohorts annually, beginning in winter, spring, and fall each year.

The 2026 schedule is as follows:

  • 26A – 26 January 2026 – 5 April 2026
  • 26B – 20 April 2026 – 5 July 2026
  • 26C – 14 September 2026 – 22 November 2026

Program Timeline

10-week business curriculum covering the following topics:

  • Business Model Canvas
  • Value Creation & Delivery
  • Sales
  • Marketing
  • Leveraging Technology
  • Communications/Public Relations
  • Financial Reports
  • Strategic Planning for Launch & Growth

Live Weekly Speaker Series (webinar led by a Subject Matter Expert) – Mondays at 2pm ET

Choosing Your Track

When applying, identify the track that best fit your needs as an entrepreneur, whether your goal is to grow your network of peers at a similar revenue stage, build a support system of entrepreneurs with shared experiences, or make connections within your industry. Participants are required to attend and actively engage in their track’s Founders Exchange.

Track Options and Founders Exchange Times

  • Women Founders
    • Tuesday – 11:00am ET
  • Black Founders
    • Tuesday – 1:00pm ET
  • Seed stage – pre-revenue with capital investments
    • Tuesday – 2:30pm ET
  • Latinx Founders
    • Wednesdays – 12:30pm ET
  • Asian American, Pacific Islander, and Native Islander Founders (AAPI/NI)
    • Wednesday – 2:00pm ET
  • Startup stage – revenue-generating up to $250k
    • Thursday – 1:30pm ET
  • Construction Skilled Trades – all business stages
    • Thursday – 2:30pm ET
  • Non Profit Founders 
    • Friday – 11:00am ET

*If you are eligible for more than one track, review the office hours times for each and select the one that aligns best with your availability. If you indicate an interest in more than one track, final placement will be determined by the IVMF team.

Cohort members are expected to keep program access exclusive to participants. Sharing program links with individuals who are not enrolled in the program is strictly prohibited. If you would like to invite a business partner to attend and participate in the cohort, you must seek prior approval from the Military Founders Lab program team. Business partners are required to submit an application, meet eligibility requirements, and be accepted into the cohort before they are permitted to engage in any program activities

Overview

Who

Veteran, military spouse, and military family founders of businesses already generating revenue or that have already fundraised for startup/growth operations.

What

Military Founders Lab is a 10-week virtual program divided into program tracks that align participants by shared experiences or industries to create a tailored support system and stronger connections within each cohort.

Where

The IVMF Military Founders Lab is a live online program experience, empowering participants to engage from anywhere with a reliable internet connection.

When

Military Founders Lab operates three cohorts annually. Each virtual cohort runs for ten weeks. New cohorts begin every winter, spring, and fall.

Why

The IVMF Military Founders Lab provides an opportunity to better equip early-stage and startup businesses for success and sustainability with expert guidance, accountability, resources, and a strong community behind you.

FAQ

Questions? View our FAQ.

Team Members

Rosie-Lee-2025-web

Rosie Lee

Program Manager | Entrepreneurship and Small Business rlee57@syr.edu
haley-chapman-2025

Haley Chapman

Program Coordinator | Entrepreneurship & Small Business hmchapma@syr.edu
Lexi-Jones_web

Lexie Jones

Program Coordinator | Entrepreneurship & Small Business ajone101@syr.edu

In Partnership With:

FAQ

  • Who is eligible to participate?
    • Active-duty, veterans, reservists, national guard, military and veteran spouses/life partners/adult dependents/caregivers.
    • Must present documentation of honorable service for self, spouse, partner, parent, or veteran receiving care.
    • All eras and all service branches are eligible.
    • Has been actively engaged in business development and operations for 6+ months
    • Operates a registered business (e.g., sole proprietorship, partnership, LLC, corporation, or nonprofit)
    • Has generated less than $250K in revenue over the past 12 months or not generating revenue but have capital investment (bootstrapped or investor-provided) to fund startup and growth operations

  • What kind of commitment does the program require?
    • Approximate time commitment of 5-8 hours per week
    • Attend and actively engage in the weekly Speaker Series
    • Complete weekly assignments that align with the webinar content and support business growth
    • Participate in weekly Founders Exchange with assigned founder track
    • Complete participant surveys throughout the program

  • Is the program virtual? In person? Hybrid?

    Virtual.

  • How big is each cohort?
    • Full cohorts will range from 75 – 230 participants
    • Cohorts tracks will have the following participant limits:
      • AAPI/NI Founders – 30 max
      • Black Founders – 30 max
      • Women Founders – 30 max
      • Latinx Founders – 30 max
      • Skilled Trades – 30 max
      • Seed Stage – 30 max
      • Startup Stage – 50 max
      • Non Profit – 30 Max

  • Are there fees?

    No.

  • Do I need to be a military veteran to apply?

    You must be one of the following: active-duty, veteran, reservist, national guard, military or veteran spouse/life partner/adult dependent/caregiver with documentation of honorable service for self, spouse, partner, parent, or veteran receiving care. All eras and all service branches are eligible.

  • I’ve already participated in Veterans in Residence, Bunker Build Up, Breaking Barriers in Entrepreneurship. Can I apply to Military Founders Lab?

    Yes, you can apply!

  • How can I contact IVMF’s Military Founders Lab?

    The Online Programs team manages the Military Founders Lab program.

    • Rosie Lee – Military Founders Lab Program Manager 
      • rlee57@syr.edu
    • Haley Chapman – Military Founders Lab Program Coordinator
      • hmchapma@syr.edu
    • Lexie Jones – Military Founders Lab Program Coordinator
      • ajone101@syr.edu

  • What happened to the Breaking Barriers in Entrepreneurship (BBiE) program?

    The Breaking Barriers in Entrepreneurship (BBiE) program has been sunsetted and integrated into the Military Founders Lab. In response to participant feedback, the Military Founders Lab offers a more robust and scalable experience—featuring expanded workshops, office hours, and peer support. By combining the structure of the Veterans in Residence program with BBiE’s inclusive mission, it better serves military-connected entrepreneurs from historically underserved communities.

     

  • What happened to the Veterans in Residence program?

    The Veterans in Residence (ViR) program has been sunsetted and replaced by the Military Founders Lab. Building on the foundation and best practices of ViR, the new program introduces specialized tracks to better support the diverse needs of military-connected entrepreneurs with more targeted resources and guidance.

  • Can my business partners join with me?

    Cohort members are expected to keep program access exclusive to participants. Sharing program links with individuals who are not enrolled in the program is strictly prohibited. If you would like to invite a business partner to attend and participate in the cohort, you must seek prior approval from the Military Founders Lab program team. Business partners are required to submit an application, meet eligibility requirements, and be accepted into the cohort before they are permitted to engage in any program activities.

page_title: Ambassador Program - D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families
main_html:
Building Business Ecosystems

The Ambassador Program unites entrepreneurial community builders from across the country with a mission to enhance local business ecosystems. The 12-month program trains and supports already well-positioned and established leaders as they engineer more friendly business environments for veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs and connect them with key entrepreneurial resources.

Our Ambassadors know the lay of the local business landscape, have an innate talent for networking, and a passion for helping veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs. Over the course of a year, they host local  networking events, to get military affiliated entrepreneurs connected to the right people and resources that can take their business to the next level. They also complete an Ecosystem Leadership Project (ELP) driving positive and lasting changes in their local business environment.

Interested in becoming an Ambassador and supporting fellow veteran and spouses? Fill out our interest form!

Ambassador Qualifications

  • Community Builder Mindset: Our Ambassadors focus on the needs of veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs, working not only to support their individual growth, but to create an environment that makes it easier for them to succeed.
  • Strong Commitment: Ambassadors demonstrate the strongest commitment, investing about five hours of effort a week throughout the year long program, and attending monthly virtual huddles and two fly-in events for training and problem-solving.
  • Resourceful Leadership: Our Ambassadors know how to excel at leading and problem-solving with the resources at hand. Most have leadership experience from their time in the military, running their own company, or working at a nonprofit.
  • Well-Positioned: Our Ambassadors have a strong network and know how to access the people and resources that can help local entrepreneurs thrive.

Find a community near you!

Why Become an Ambassador?

Becoming an Ambassador is an incredible opportunity for leaders who understand and value the power of community, having experienced its benefits firsthand. Ambassadors have access to valuable entrepreneurial resources and networks and are eager to share them with others, paying it forward. In this role, you’ll be at the intersection of veterans, military spouses, and entrepreneurship within your community.

Representing IVMF, a well-respected national nonprofit, will open new doors that might have otherwise remained closed. Being an Ambassador gives you an opportunity to supercharge your own network, not just by being in the room with key players in your local ecosystem, but by creating the guest list yourself. Further, if you’re part of an entrepreneurial service organization (ESO) or run a business that supports other companies, serving as an Ambassador can greatly enhance your ability to serve even more people. Key ecosystem partners make outstanding Ambassadors and can benefit from a broader view of the local entrepreneurial landscape.

Ecosystem Leadership Project (ELP)

As an Ambassador, you become a steward and caretaker of your local entrepreneurial environment. The Ecosystem Leadership Project (ELP) is a unique initiative designed by each Ambassador to make the local business community more accessible for veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs and small business owners.

An ELP can take many forms. Ambassadors might plan and host networking events that gives veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs an opportunity to meet with investors or mentors. Other Ambassadors might curate a comprehensive ecosystem map of local resources. Each project is tailored to marry the Ambassadors the skills and knowledge of the Ambassadors to address the needs of local veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs. Regardless of the form it takes, every ELP aims to create lasting improvements in the accessibility of entrepreneurial resources for local veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs.

Interested in Becoming An Ambassador

Program Overview

WHO

Volunteers passionate about creating a more opportunity-filled business environment for veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs and small business owners.

WHERE

Two fly-in events filled with ecosystem building training, along with monthly virtual huddles.

WHEN

The mandatory 2026 fly-in event are scheduled for July 28th – July 31st, 2026. Our 2027 fly-in is TBD. There are also monthly virtual connections.

WHY

Supercharge your network and put it to good use serving veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs by connecting them with key contacts and resources to launch and grow their businesses.

Alumni Testimonials

Slide 1

Since I’ve been with the ambassador program, my network has changed and I’ve connected with so many different people and customers.

Nathaniel Torres
Co-Founder, Lavi

One of the benefits of being an Ambassador is being able to find ways to help one another and find resources and tools we can offer to each other.

Monica Fullerton
Founder, Spouse-ly

As an Ambassador, you get to help people overcome challenges and struggles and see those you’ve helped, help others.

Brandon Aaron
Co-Founder, Highr1

What I find most exciting about being involved with the Ambassador program is reconnecting with fellow veterans and other people who have similar experiences. It’s something I’ve missed dearly since checking out of the military.

Doug Bauer
Founder, Serac Technologies

Creating Opportunity

Joining the Ambassador Program allows you to make a real difference in the lives of veterans and military spouses. Local Ambassadors play a huge role in and helping them actualize their American dreams of entrepreneurship and small business ownership by fostering a more friendly business ecosystem, and expanding their access to resources and networks.

The Ambassador Program is your chance to be the person who makes that key introduction or points an entrepreneur to that critical resource that can change their lives and the trajectory of their business. Early-stage founders can get caught up in their day-to-day operations that they miss big picture opportunities sitting right next to them. As an Ambassador, your ability to raise awareness about those opportunities and facilitate connections is an invaluable part of their journey, and one they’ll never forget.

Frequently Asked Questions

  • Who is eligible to participate?

    Anyone with a passion for helping veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs is eligible to apply. However, the best candidates will also be well-positioned within the local business ecosystem to help veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs, or have unique access to a network or resource that can help them launch and grow their companies.     

  • Do you have to be an existing member of the Ambassador community to apply?

    Prior IVMF participation or engagement is not required, but we hold those already engaged with our community in high regard.

  • What kind of commitment does the program require?

    5 hours per week on average. This is a volunteer position and may require some evening and weekend work to attend community events. The Ambassador will need to have access to their own transportation to travel to various events and meetings. Physical Requirements: The Ambassador will be required to stand or sit for extended periods and may need to lift or move light objects during event setup.

  • Which cities have the program?

    IVMF is always looking to expand to different cities, and Ambassadors are an important first step to developing the local ecosystem to support veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs. Cities with an active Veterans in Residence cohort will take precedence, but if you think your city is ready, apply to be an Ambassador today, and let’s start developing the local community together!

  • Does IVMF make investments in Ambassador cohort businesses?

    No

  • Do I need to be a military veteran to apply?

    No, you don’t necessarily have to be a veteran to be an Ambassador, you just need to have a passion for helping people and enjoy networking and problem-solving.  Applicants should self-identify as servant leaders who are dedicated to supporting the veteran and military spouse entrepreneur community. This means they should prioritize the needs of others, aim to enhance the growth and well-being of community members, and work towards building a more collaborative network that is locally thriving and nationally connected.

  • I was rejected from the program in the past. Can I apply again?

    Yes, we encourage you to apply again and to consider other IVMF programming that may be a fit for you including EBV , VWISE, Veteran Edge, CEOcircle, and Military Founders Lab.  

  • What are the criteria of competitive candidates?
    • The best candidates will be dedicated servant leaders that are well-positioned within the local business ecosystem to help veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs, or have unique access to a network or resource that can help IVMF entrepreneurs launch and grow their companies. 
    • However, IVMF is also looking for candidates with:  
    • Strong leadership and communication skills.
    • Experience in networking and ecosystem building.
    • Knowledge of local entrepreneurial resources.
    • Passionate about supporting military-connected entrepreneurs.
    • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
    • Commitment to the volunteer role for at least 12 months.
    • Willingness to participate in IVMF Ambassador training.
    • Skilled at making beneficial referrals that can benefit both parties and lead to positive outcomes.
    • Skilled at identifying opportunities and engaging with key stakeholders in the industry or community to build partnerships or networks.
    • Relevant education or experience in business, entrepreneurship, economic development, marketing, communications, public administration, nonprofit management, and ecosystem building.
    • Experience in organizing and hosting events.
    • Familiarity with the needs and challenges faced by military-connected entrepreneurs.
    • Experience in entrepreneurship or startup development.
    • Active in the local veteran or entrepreneur community.
    • Veteran or military spouse a plus, but not required.

  • What’s in it for me?
    • An opportunity to be of service to veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs trying to realize their American Dream.
    • Supercharge your network while connecting up-and-coming military connected entrepreneurs with the local entrepreneurial ecosystem.
    • Access to a vibrant community that offers a strong sense of camaraderie and community amongst veteran and military spouses
    • Recognition as a local leader driving economic development.
    • Two fully covered in-person fly-in training events that teach skills like ecosystem building, networking, and mentorship.

  • Is travel involved?

    Yes. The program will cover your travel expenses for the Ambassador Program’s two fly-in training events.

  • The next cohort doesn’t start for months, what can I do in the meantime?

    Reach out to the current Ambassadors in your city, and attend any IVMF events in your area.

Further, if you’re part of an entrepreneurial service organization (ESO) or run a business that supports other companies, serving as an Ambassador can greatly enhance your ability to serve even more people. Key ecosystem partners make outstanding Ambassadors and can benefit from a broader view of the local entrepreneurial landscape. Ecosystem Leadership Project (ELP) As an Ambassador, you become a steward and caretaker of your local entrepreneurial environment. The Ecosystem Leadership Project (ELP) is a unique initiative designed by each Ambassador to make the local business community more accessible for veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs and small business owners. An ELP can take many forms. Ambassadors might plan and host networking events that gives veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs an opportunity to meet with investors or mentors. Other Ambassadors might curate a comprehensive ecosystem map of local resources. Each project is tailored to marry the Ambassadors the skills and knowledge of the Ambassadors to address the needs of local veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs. Regardless of the form it takes, every ELP aims to create lasting improvements in the accessibility of entrepreneurial resources for local veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs. ﻿ Interested in Becoming An Ambassador Program Overview WHO Volunteers passionate about creating a more opportunity-filled business environment for veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs and small business owners. WHERE Two fly-in events filled with ecosystem building training, along with monthly virtual huddles. WHEN The mandatory 2026 fly-in event are scheduled for July 28th – July 31st, 2026. Our 2027 fly-in is TBD. There are also monthly virtual connections. WHY Supercharge your network and put it to good use serving veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs by connecting them with key contacts and resources to launch and grow their businesses. Alumni Testimonials Slide 1 Since I’ve been with the ambassador program, my network has changed and I’ve connected with so many different people and customers. Nathaniel Torres Co-Founder, Lavi One of the benefits of being an Ambassador is being able to find ways to help one another and find resources and tools we can offer to each other. Monica Fullerton Founder, Spouse-ly As an Ambassador, you get to help people overcome challenges and struggles and see those you’ve helped, help others. Brandon Aaron Co-Founder, Highr1 What I find most exciting about being involved with the Ambassador program is reconnecting with fellow veterans and other people who have similar experiences. It’s something I’ve missed dearly since checking out of the military. Doug Bauer Founder, Serac Technologies Creating Opportunity Joining the Ambassador Program allows you to make a real difference in the lives of veterans and military spouses. Local Ambassadors play a huge role in and helping them actualize their American dreams of entrepreneurship and small business ownership by fostering a more friendly business ecosystem, and expanding their access to resources and networks. The Ambassador Program is your chance to be the person who makes that key introduction or points an entrepreneur to that critical resource that can change their lives and the trajectory of their business. Early-stage founders can get caught up in their day-to-day operations that they miss big picture opportunities sitting right next to them. As an Ambassador, your ability to raise awareness about those opportunities and facilitate connections is an invaluable part of their journey, and one they’ll never forget. Frequently Asked Questions Who is eligible to participate? Anyone with a passion for helping veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs is eligible to apply. However, the best candidates will also be well-positioned within the local business ecosystem to help veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs, or have unique access to a network or resource that can help them launch and grow their companies. Do you have to be an existing member of the Ambassador community to apply? Prior IVMF participation or engagement is not required, but we hold those already engaged with our community in high regard. What kind of commitment does the program require? 5 hours per week on average. This is a volunteer position and may require some evening and weekend work to attend community events. The Ambassador will need to have access to their own transportation to travel to various events and meetings. Physical Requirements: The Ambassador will be required to stand or sit for extended periods and may need to lift or move light objects during event setup. Which cities have the program? IVMF is always looking to expand to different cities, and Ambassadors are an important first step to developing the local ecosystem to support veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs. Cities with an active Veterans in Residence cohort will take precedence, but if you think your city is ready, apply to be an Ambassador today, and let’s start developing the local community together! Does IVMF make investments in Ambassador cohort businesses? No Do I need to be a military veteran to apply? No, you don’t necessarily have to be a veteran to be an Ambassador, you just need to have a passion for helping people and enjoy networking and problem-solving. Applicants should self-identify as servant leaders who are dedicated to supporting the veteran and military spouse entrepreneur community. This means they should prioritize the needs of others, aim to enhance the growth and well-being of community members, and work towards building a more collaborative network that is locally thriving and nationally connected. I was rejected from the program in the past. Can I apply again? Yes, we encourage you to apply again and to consider other IVMF programming that may be a fit for you including EBV , VWISE , Veteran Edge , CEOcircle , and Military Founders Lab . What are the criteria of competitive candidates? The best candidates will be dedicated servant leaders that are well-positioned within the local business ecosystem to help veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs, or have unique access to a network or resource that can help IVMF entrepreneurs launch and grow their companies. However, IVMF is also looking for candidates with: Strong leadership and communication skills. Experience in networking and ecosystem building. Knowledge of local entrepreneurial resources. Passionate about supporting military-connected entrepreneurs. Ability to work independently and as part of a team. Commitment to the volunteer role for at least 12 months. Willingness to participate in IVMF Ambassador training. Skilled at making beneficial referrals that can benefit both parties and lead to positive outcomes. Skilled at identifying opportunities and engaging with key stakeholders in the industry or community to build partnerships or networks. Relevant education or experience in business, entrepreneurship, economic development, marketing, communications, public administration, nonprofit management, and ecosystem building. Experience in organizing and hosting events. Familiarity with the needs and challenges faced by military-connected entrepreneurs. Experience in entrepreneurship or startup development. Active in the local veteran or entrepreneur community. Veteran or military spouse a plus, but not required. What’s in it for me? An opportunity to be of service to veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs trying to realize their American Dream. Supercharge your network while connecting up-and-coming military connected entrepreneurs with the local entrepreneurial ecosystem. Access to a vibrant community that offers a strong sense of camaraderie and community amongst veteran and military spouses Recognition as a local leader driving economic development. Two fully covered in-person fly-in training events that teach skills like ecosystem building, networking, and mentorship. Is travel involved? Yes. The program will cover your travel expenses for the Ambassador Program’s two fly-in training events. The next cohort doesn’t start for months, what can I do in the meantime? Reach out to the current Ambassadors in your city, and attend any IVMF events in your area.

page_title: CEOcircle - D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families
main_html:
Join an Executive Cohort

CEOcircle is a monthly peer accountability group for growth-stage companies looking to scale. Over the course of nine virtual huddles and four in person fly-in forum events, CEOs and executives can ask critical questions impacting their businesses today. Together, you’ll learn from your peers and national experts alike how to take your company to the next level. Progress through the program is focused and measured based off self-set goals and helped by intentional and facilitated connections. Additionally, CEOcircle members also gain access to dedicated JPMorgan Chase Commercial Banking liaisons.

CEOcircle cohort members are divided into call sign groups, where similar stage and revenue level companies build lifelong relationships and support each other through regular business challenges.

Our world-class fly-in events include tailored talks from national-profile business leaders. Previous speakers have included Larry Johnson (Former CEO, Fogo De Chão), Kelly Perdew (Managing Partner, Moonshots Capital), Nancy Minchillo (Vice President, Global Supplier Diversity, JPMorgan Chase & Co.), Chris Cassidy (CEO & President, National Medal of Honor Museum, former Navy SEAL and astronaut) and more.

Who is eligible?

  • Applicant must be a military veteran and/or military spouse 
  • CEO, senior level executive and/or controlling shareholder of company
  • Company grosses $1MIL+ OR has raised $5MIL+ in capital 
  • Company shows high growth potential including: 
    • Market Size 
    • Industry 
    • Market Saturation 
    • Significant Traction

What industries qualify?

All industries welcome to apply. Industries might include but are not limited to government contracting, healthcare, manufacturing, marketing, etc. 

Previous participants have been in the following industries and more

  • Government Contracting
  • Technology & Scientific Services
  • Healthcare & Public Services
  • B2C – CPG; Retail; Restaurant

Interested in the next Cohort? Fill out the interest form today!

Program Criteria

CEOcircle is for veteran and military spouse CEOs and executives driving significant investment ($5+ million USD) or revenue ($1+ million USD) seeking a real peer network of executives running companies at similar stages and revenue levels.

Presented by:

Details

Who

Veteran and military spouse CEOs and executives driving significant investment ($5+ million USD) or revenue ($1+ million USD) seeking a real peer network of executives running companies at similar stages and revenue levels.

What

A monthly accountability group consisting of industry peers challenging each other to grow and facing the trials of modern business together.

Where

Monthly virtual huddles, with quarterly fly-in events packed with programming and unique educational, business, and networking opportunities.

When

CEOcircle meets once a month for 13 months, beginning in November through November of the following year. The application process is open June through August of the same year.

Why

Take advantage of a unique entrepreneurship brain-trust packed with Veteran and military spouse peers at similar stages of growth. Learn from national-profile business leaders.

FAQ

Questions? View our FAQ

Why CEOCircle?

There are a lot of “mastermind” programs out there, but CEOcircle is the only one exclusive to Veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs. Every single member of your cohort isn’t just your peer in terms of running a successful business. They also have a story of their own service, and can relate to your story and speak your language. They are also seeking tactical, tangible steps to solving the challenges their businesses are facing.

Frequently Asked Questions

  • Who is eligible to participate?

    Veteran and military spouse CEOs and executives driving significant investment ($5+ million USD) or revenue ($1+ million USD) seeking a real peer network of executives running companies at similar stages and revenue levels.  

  • What does significant traction mean?

    Markers of success vary by industry. For example, a device maker’s traction might be measured in the number of devices sold, whereas a media company might measure traction in terms of subscriptions or ad revenue.

  • What kind of commitment does the program require?

    A year-long commitment, consisting of monthly meetings. In some cohorts, quarterly travel is required to meet in-person as a group.

    Participants will have 9 monthly 90-minute meetings. In addition to the monthly meetings, the program will consist of 4 in-person fly-in forums held throughout the year in various locations around the US. The fly-in forums will include a short program session and evening social event followed by a full day of programming that will include breakout sessions, high profile speakers and intentional facilitation.

  • Which cities have the program?

    All cohorts are virtual, and participants can be located anywhere.

  • How big is each cohort?

    There are typically 10-12 entrepreneurs per group.

  • Are there any fees?

    No, but as the participant, you cover travel and lodging for each fly-in forum. Once you arrive, food and refreshments will all be provided throughout the event. We will have discounted room rates at a hotel near the venue in the form of a room block.

  • How are participants selected?

    Fill out an application to indicate your interest in being considered, or sign up on the wait-list if applications are not currently open. Participants are vetted by industry-specific success metrics to ensure the cohort is a true peer-group.

  • Does IVMF make investments in cohort businesses?

    No. This program does not include any type of funding. We hope that the progress and goals you accomplish during the program will move your company forward to reach follow-on goals like future fundraising efforts. This program will amplify your network and acumen to grow your business.

  • Do I need to be a military veteran to apply?

    Participants must be Veterans or military spouses.

  • I was rejected from the program in the past. Can I apply again?

    Yes, please do. If you were rejected because of revenue requirements, note this round the revenue criteria is $1MIL or company has raised $5MIL+ in capital. If your company isn’t quite there yet, Veterans in Residence program might be a better fit.

  • What are the criteria of competitive candidates?
    • Applicant must be a military Veteran and/or military spouse
    • CEO, senior level executive and/or controlling shareholder of company
    • Company grosses $1MIL+ OR Company has raised $5MIL+ in capital
    • Company shows high growth potential including
      • Market Size
      • Industry
      • Market Saturation
      • Significant Traction

  • Why is there an emphasis on participants’ success metrics?

    Bunker Labs offers a range of programs designed to serve entrepreneurs and business owners at specific points of the entrepreneurial journey. The needs of an entrepreneur with an idea or a brand new startup are very different from that of an entrepreneur who is, for example, overseeing expansions of their product into new geographic markets. Offering targeted programming helps us keep each program relevant and effective for the entrepreneurs and business owners who participate.

Founding Partner

page_title: Military Founders Lab - D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families
meta_description: Military Founders Lab is a 10-week virtual program delivers immediate, practical impact with access to business tools, resources, mentorship, and a strong peer network for veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs.
main_html:
Formerly the Veterans in Residence (ViR), Breaking Barriers in Entrepreneurship (BBiE), and Bunker Build Up (BBU) programs, IVMF has streamlined and combined these three programs into the Military Founders Lab. Over 10-weeks, this virtual program delivers immediate, practical impact and support for business growth and development with access to business tools, resources, mentorship, and a strong peer network. Military Founders Lab also provides multiple tracks that align participants by shared experiences or industries, creating a tailored support system and stronger connections within each cohort.

What You Will Experience

  • Build and develop business knowledge and management skills
  • Increase confidence to grow a viable, sustainable business
  • Learn about resources and tools to accelerate business growth
  • Expand professional network among like-minded, veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs at a similar stage of business

Eligibility

  • Active-duty, veterans, reservists, guard, military and veteran spouses/life partners/adult dependents/caregivers.
  • All must present documentation of honorable service for self, spouse, partner, parent, or veteran receiving care.
  • All eras and all service branches are eligible.

Applicants must also meet the following business requirements:

  • Have been actively working on business development and operations for at least six months.
  • Have a registered business in their state of operations, including sole proprietorship, partnership, LLC, corporation, or nonprofit organization.
  • Generating revenue under $250K in the last 12 months or not generating revenue but have capital investment (bootstrapped or investor-provided) to fund startup and growth operations.

Program Details

Participants in the Military Founders Lab will actively engage in two virtual meetings per week, accompanied by structured weekly coursework. The Speaker Series (live webinar led by a Subject Matter Expert) is held on Mondays at 2pm ET and is recorded for asynchronous review if needed. If a participant is not able to attend and engage in the Speaker Series live, they are required to review the recording after the fact. The Founders Exchange (live virtual office hour) is track-specific and must be attended and engaged with live – they are not recorded. Participants are required to attend and engage with at least five live Founders Exchange sessions over the course of 10 weeks.

Upcoming Cohorts

There are three, 10-week, Military Founders Lab cohorts annually, beginning in winter, spring, and fall each year.

The 2026 schedule is as follows:

  • 26A – 26 January 2026 – 5 April 2026
  • 26B – 20 April 2026 – 5 July 2026
  • 26C – 14 September 2026 – 22 November 2026

Program Timeline

10-week business curriculum covering the following topics:

  • Business Model Canvas
  • Value Creation & Delivery
  • Sales
  • Marketing
  • Leveraging Technology
  • Communications/Public Relations
  • Financial Reports
  • Strategic Planning for Launch & Growth

Live Weekly Speaker Series (webinar led by a Subject Matter Expert) – Mondays at 2pm ET

Choosing Your Track

When applying, identify the track that best fit your needs as an entrepreneur, whether your goal is to grow your network of peers at a similar revenue stage, build a support system of entrepreneurs with shared experiences, or make connections within your industry. Participants are required to attend and actively engage in their track’s Founders Exchange.

Track Options and Founders Exchange Times

  • Women Founders
    • Tuesday – 11:00am ET
  • Black Founders
    • Tuesday – 1:00pm ET
  • Seed stage – pre-revenue with capital investments
    • Tuesday – 2:30pm ET
  • Latinx Founders
    • Wednesdays – 12:30pm ET
  • Asian American, Pacific Islander, and Native Islander Founders (AAPI/NI)
    • Wednesday – 2:00pm ET
  • Startup stage – revenue-generating up to $250k
    • Thursday – 1:30pm ET
  • Construction Skilled Trades – all business stages
    • Thursday – 2:30pm ET
  • Non Profit Founders 
    • Friday – 11:00am ET

*If you are eligible for more than one track, review the office hours times for each and select the one that aligns best with your availability. If you indicate an interest in more than one track, final placement will be determined by the IVMF team.

Cohort members are expected to keep program access exclusive to participants. Sharing program links with individuals who are not enrolled in the program is strictly prohibited. If you would like to invite a business partner to attend and participate in the cohort, you must seek prior approval from the Military Founders Lab program team. Business partners are required to submit an application, meet eligibility requirements, and be accepted into the cohort before they are permitted to engage in any program activities

Overview

Who

Veteran, military spouse, and military family founders of businesses already generating revenue or that have already fundraised for startup/growth operations.

What

Military Founders Lab is a 10-week virtual program divided into program tracks that align participants by shared experiences or industries to create a tailored support system and stronger connections within each cohort.

Where

The IVMF Military Founders Lab is a live online program experience, empowering participants to engage from anywhere with a reliable internet connection.

When

Military Founders Lab operates three cohorts annually. Each virtual cohort runs for ten weeks. New cohorts begin every winter, spring, and fall.

Why

The IVMF Military Founders Lab provides an opportunity to better equip early-stage and startup businesses for success and sustainability with expert guidance, accountability, resources, and a strong community behind you.

FAQ

Questions? View our FAQ.

FAQ

  • Who is eligible to participate?
    • Active-duty, veterans, reservists, national guard, military and veteran spouses/life partners/adult dependents/caregivers.
    • Must present documentation of honorable service for self, spouse, partner, parent, or veteran receiving care.
    • All eras and all service branches are eligible.
    • Has been actively engaged in business development and operations for 6+ months
    • Operates a registered business (e.g., sole proprietorship, partnership, LLC, corporation, or nonprofit)
    • Has generated less than $250K in revenue over the past 12 months or not generating revenue but have capital investment (bootstrapped or investor-provided) to fund startup and growth operations

  • What kind of commitment does the program require?
    • Approximate time commitment of 5-8 hours per week
    • Attend and actively engage in the weekly Speaker Series
    • Complete weekly assignments that align with the webinar content and support business growth
    • Participate in weekly Founders Exchange with assigned founder track
    • Complete participant surveys throughout the program

  • Is the program virtual? In person? Hybrid?

    Virtual.

  • How big is each cohort?
    • Full cohorts will range from 75 – 230 participants
    • Cohorts tracks will have the following participant limits:
      • AAPI/NI Founders – 30 max
      • Black Founders – 30 max
      • Women Founders – 30 max
      • Latinx Founders – 30 max
      • Skilled Trades – 30 max
      • Seed Stage – 30 max
      • Startup Stage – 50 max
      • Non Profit – 30 Max

  • Are there fees?

    No.

  • Do I need to be a military veteran to apply?

    You must be one of the following: active-duty, veteran, reservist, national guard, military or veteran spouse/life partner/adult dependent/caregiver with documentation of honorable service for self, spouse, partner, parent, or veteran receiving care. All eras and all service branches are eligible.

  • I’ve already participated in Veterans in Residence, Bunker Build Up, Breaking Barriers in Entrepreneurship. Can I apply to Military Founders Lab?

    Yes, you can apply!

  • How can I contact IVMF’s Military Founders Lab?

    The Online Programs team manages the Military Founders Lab program.

    • Rosie Lee – Military Founders Lab Program Manager 
      • rlee57@syr.edu
    • Haley Chapman – Military Founders Lab Program Coordinator
      • hmchapma@syr.edu
    • Lexie Jones – Military Founders Lab Program Coordinator
      • ajone101@syr.edu

  • What happened to the Breaking Barriers in Entrepreneurship (BBiE) program?

    The Breaking Barriers in Entrepreneurship (BBiE) program has been sunsetted and integrated into the Military Founders Lab. In response to participant feedback, the Military Founders Lab offers a more robust and scalable experience—featuring expanded workshops, office hours, and peer support. By combining the structure of the Veterans in Residence program with BBiE’s inclusive mission, it better serves military-connected entrepreneurs from historically underserved communities.

     

  • What happened to the Veterans in Residence program?

    The Veterans in Residence (ViR) program has been sunsetted and replaced by the Military Founders Lab. Building on the foundation and best practices of ViR, the new program introduces specialized tracks to better support the diverse needs of military-connected entrepreneurs with more targeted resources and guidance.

  • Can my business partners join with me?

    Cohort members are expected to keep program access exclusive to participants. Sharing program links with individuals who are not enrolled in the program is strictly prohibited. If you would like to invite a business partner to attend and participate in the cohort, you must seek prior approval from the Military Founders Lab program team. Business partners are required to submit an application, meet eligibility requirements, and be accepted into the cohort before they are permitted to engage in any program activities.

page_title: Military Founders Lab - D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families
meta_description: Military Founders Lab is a 10-week virtual program delivers immediate, practical impact with access to business tools, resources, mentorship, and a strong peer network for veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs.
main_html:
Formerly the Veterans in Residence (ViR), Breaking Barriers in Entrepreneurship (BBiE), and Bunker Build Up (BBU) programs, IVMF has streamlined and combined these three programs into the Military Founders Lab. Over 10-weeks, this virtual program delivers immediate, practical impact and support for business growth and development with access to business tools, resources, mentorship, and a strong peer network. Military Founders Lab also provides multiple tracks that align participants by shared experiences or industries, creating a tailored support system and stronger connections within each cohort.

What You Will Experience

  • Build and develop business knowledge and management skills
  • Increase confidence to grow a viable, sustainable business
  • Learn about resources and tools to accelerate business growth
  • Expand professional network among like-minded, veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs at a similar stage of business

Eligibility

  • Active-duty, veterans, reservists, guard, military and veteran spouses/life partners/adult dependents/caregivers.
  • All must present documentation of honorable service for self, spouse, partner, parent, or veteran receiving care.
  • All eras and all service branches are eligible.

Applicants must also meet the following business requirements:

  • Have been actively working on business development and operations for at least six months.
  • Have a registered business in their state of operations, including sole proprietorship, partnership, LLC, corporation, or nonprofit organization.
  • Generating revenue under $250K in the last 12 months or not generating revenue but have capital investment (bootstrapped or investor-provided) to fund startup and growth operations.

Program Details

Participants in the Military Founders Lab will actively engage in two virtual meetings per week, accompanied by structured weekly coursework. The Speaker Series (live webinar led by a Subject Matter Expert) is held on Mondays at 2pm ET and is recorded for asynchronous review if needed. If a participant is not able to attend and engage in the Speaker Series live, they are required to review the recording after the fact. The Founders Exchange (live virtual office hour) is track-specific and must be attended and engaged with live – they are not recorded. Participants are required to attend and engage with at least five live Founders Exchange sessions over the course of 10 weeks.

Upcoming Cohorts

There are three, 10-week, Military Founders Lab cohorts annually, beginning in winter, spring, and fall each year.

The 2026 schedule is as follows:

  • 26A – 26 January 2026 – 5 April 2026
  • 26B – 20 April 2026 – 5 July 2026
  • 26C – 14 September 2026 – 22 November 2026

Program Timeline

10-week business curriculum covering the following topics:

  • Business Model Canvas
  • Value Creation & Delivery
  • Sales
  • Marketing
  • Leveraging Technology
  • Communications/Public Relations
  • Financial Reports
  • Strategic Planning for Launch & Growth

Live Weekly Speaker Series (webinar led by a Subject Matter Expert) – Mondays at 2pm ET

Choosing Your Track

When applying, identify the track that best fit your needs as an entrepreneur, whether your goal is to grow your network of peers at a similar revenue stage, build a support system of entrepreneurs with shared experiences, or make connections within your industry. Participants are required to attend and actively engage in their track’s Founders Exchange.

Track Options and Founders Exchange Times

  • Women Founders
    • Tuesday – 11:00am ET
  • Black Founders
    • Tuesday – 1:00pm ET
  • Seed stage – pre-revenue with capital investments
    • Tuesday – 2:30pm ET
  • Latinx Founders
    • Wednesdays – 12:30pm ET
  • Asian American, Pacific Islander, and Native Islander Founders (AAPI/NI)
    • Wednesday – 2:00pm ET
  • Startup stage – revenue-generating up to $250k
    • Thursday – 1:30pm ET
  • Construction Skilled Trades – all business stages
    • Thursday – 2:30pm ET
  • Non Profit Founders 
    • Friday – 11:00am ET

*If you are eligible for more than one track, review the office hours times for each and select the one that aligns best with your availability. If you indicate an interest in more than one track, final placement will be determined by the IVMF team.

Cohort members are expected to keep program access exclusive to participants. Sharing program links with individuals who are not enrolled in the program is strictly prohibited. If you would like to invite a business partner to attend and participate in the cohort, you must seek prior approval from the Military Founders Lab program team. Business partners are required to submit an application, meet eligibility requirements, and be accepted into the cohort before they are permitted to engage in any program activities

Overview

Who

Veteran, military spouse, and military family founders of businesses already generating revenue or that have already fundraised for startup/growth operations.

What

Military Founders Lab is a 10-week virtual program divided into program tracks that align participants by shared experiences or industries to create a tailored support system and stronger connections within each cohort.

Where

The IVMF Military Founders Lab is a live online program experience, empowering participants to engage from anywhere with a reliable internet connection.

When

Military Founders Lab operates three cohorts annually. Each virtual cohort runs for ten weeks. New cohorts begin every winter, spring, and fall.

Why

The IVMF Military Founders Lab provides an opportunity to better equip early-stage and startup businesses for success and sustainability with expert guidance, accountability, resources, and a strong community behind you.

main_html:
Enhancing Veteran and Military Family Owned Businesses

About the Coalition for Veteran Owned Business

The Coalition for Veteran Owned Business (CVOB) is a group comprised of industry leaders committed to providing opportunities and growth for veteran and military spouse-owned businesses. This first-of-its-kind national initiative supports the success of veteran, service member, and military spouse-owned businesses by connecting them with entrepreneurial education and training, small business resources and solutions, and commerce and supplier opportunities to help connect and educate both sides on doing business together.

Coalition Priorities

  • Increase opportunities and information
  • Create networking opportunities
  • Create awareness of resources
  • Help form corporate connections

Support Military-Owned Business

Shop online with IVMF’s Buy Military-Owned Shopping Guide to meet all of your shopping needs with over 500 veteran-, active duty-, reservist- and military spouse-owned businesses! Shop gifts and services from all categories and add your business to the list by filling out the forms at the top of the page!

h1: Center of Excellence for Veteran Entrepreneurship (COE)
main_html:
The mission of the Center of Excellence (COE) for Veteran Entrepreneurship is to create, collect, organize, and share knowledge, resources, and networks to advance entrepreneurial opportunities for transitioning service members, veterans, and their families. This is accomplished through the development and delivery of innovative programs and educational resources; timely and relevant research and policy analysis; and by cultivating veteran-connected ecosystems across the United States.

Our Priorities

  • Research & Policy
    • Evaluate and assess research and policy
    • Organize current knowledge in the field of veteran entrepreneurship
    • Create and drive new and necessary research
    • Advocate using data to influence strategies and policies that will have a positive impact on business creation and growth for transitioning service members, veterans, and their families
    • Cultivate networks – evaluate current networks and take steps to close gaps and/or establish new networks

  • Education & Training

    • Design, develop, and deliver innovative programs
    • Create a clearinghouse for veteran-connected small business curriculum
    • Identify and disseminate best practices
    • Develop standards for veteran-connected small business programming and curriculum
    • Provide supportive services for stakeholders within the ecosystem – VOBs, employers, veteran entrepreneurship educators and others

  • Collaboration and Partnership
    • Serve as the bridge to connect all stakeholders and networks
    • Build and maintain strategic partnerships
    • Create and connect supply chain opportunities
    • Mentor VOBs and other stakeholders
    • Establish consortium of educators and small business leaders
